video_title: Lionel Hollins | Playing with Julius Erving, Coaching Tony & Zach, Addressing Deron Williams Slander

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on his early life and path to basketball
quotes.excerpt: When you're poor, you got to work. And my grandmother said, I don't care nothing about no baseball.

text_blocks.speaker: Zach Randolph
text_blocks.text: You were born in Arkansas, City, Kansas, but you moved to Las Vegas early on in your age?

text_blocks.speaker: Lionel Hollins
text_blocks.text: Four months old. I never lived in Kansas. I never lived. Okay. Yeah, so you're a Vegas, you're a Nevada baby for sure. For sure. And spent a little bit of time in Oakland, California, and also down in Compton, but not long.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: What made your family relocate to the West Coast?

text_blocks.speaker: Lionel Hollins
text_blocks.text: Well, everybody moved for jobs. People were doing that. They were moving from the South, moving from the Midwest, trying to find a consistent work. And so that was the real reason. And so we settled on Vegas, and I'm glad we did because I can't imagine living in Kansas, you know, in a city that didn't have as many people that was in my high school.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on why he stopped playing baseball
quotes.excerpt: When you're poor, you got to work. And my grandmother said, I don't care nothing about no baseball.

text_blocks.speaker: Lionel Hollins
text_blocks.text: In fact, I had dinner two years ago with my baseball coach who's 92 years old, and he still is upset that I quit playing baseball because he had a whole bunch of scouts from the major leagues looking at me. And the problem was when you're poor, you got to work. And my grandmother said, I don't care nothing about no baseball. You got to go get a job to help pay some of these bills. That ended baseball.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: And then I started growing and basketball became the dominant sport.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on his coaching philosophy and team ego
quotes.excerpt: He says, do you want to lead the state in scoring or do you want to win a championship?

text_blocks.speaker: Lionel Hollins
text_blocks.text: He says, do you want to lead the state in scoring or do you want to win a championship? I said, I want to win a championship. He said, well, your teammates there, they've never been behind you, they've always been ahead of you, and they're not going to be behind you now because this is their ego. And so he says, you got to share the ball with them and you'll win more.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: And we did.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on his early plan to escape Las Vegas
quotes.excerpt: I was going to buy me a van, I was going to get a job at one of the hotels.

text_blocks.speaker: Lionel Hollins
text_blocks.text: School wasn't for me. I was just going to get a job. But I also had a plan of how I was going to get out of Las Vegas. I was going to buy me a van, I was going to get a job at one of the hotels, either washing dishes or busting tables. That's all they allowed you to do back then. And I was going to live in my van and save all my money, and then I was going to get up and be a ghost.

text_blocks.speaker: Zach Randolph
text_blocks.text: But my high school coach says there's a school up the road in St. George, Utah, two hours away. Coach wants to give you a full ride.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on overcoming adversity and changing his mindset
quotes.excerpt: Everybody that don't look like you don't dislike you. There's some people that don't look like you going to like you more.

text_blocks.speaker: Lionel Hollins
text_blocks.text: And he says, and everybody that don't look like you don't dislike you. There's some people that don't look like you going to like you more than anybody else. And that kind of changed my truth. My mindset changed, and I learned a lot and grew a lot, and then went on to Arizona State. Things took off, and then I was a six pick in the NBA draft.

text_blocks.speaker: Zach Randolph
text_blocks.text: Yeah, and that's what I want to ask coach, like, you grew up on the West Coast, but you grew back in the time, you know, racism.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on growing up in segregated Las Vegas
quotes.excerpt: My grandmother and all of them used to call Vegas little Mississippi.

text_blocks.speaker: Lionel Hollins
text_blocks.text: My grandmother and all of them used to call Vegas little Mississippi. It was racism and segregation. We had historic Black Las Vegas, a West Side. Had our own casinos, own hotels, everything, you know. And nobody Black actually went on the other side of town unless they went to work in the kitchen.

text_blocks.speaker: Zach Randolph
text_blocks.text: And then when integration came, everybody wanted to go spend their money out there on the strip.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on his survival mindset and avoiding jail
quotes.excerpt: I had a mindset that I wasn't going to steal and I wasn't going to jail.

text_blocks.speaker: Lionel Hollins
text_blocks.text: I had a mindset that I wasn't going to steal and I wasn't going to jail. And because we had a lot of people that hung out and did that kind of stuff, and eventually I just walked away from them because I was not going to be in jail. First, I wasn't going to be handcuffed. Secondly, I wasn't going to get on the phone and say, Grandma, I'm in jail.

text_blocks.speaker: Zach Randolph
text_blocks.text: Oh my goodness. Ain't no way.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on his experience at Dixie State
quotes.excerpt: I was just trying to be me, go to school, meet people, have a good time.

text_blocks.speaker: Lionel Hollins
text_blocks.text: I was just trying to be me, go to school, meet people, have a good time. Man, you can't talk to those white people over there. You can't hang with them, you know, and they don't like us and blah, blah, blah, blah, blah, right? But I wasn't getting treated that way by everybody. There was certain people that didn't like me, but most of the people were very friendly.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: And so when they left, a weight went off my back because now I could grow as a person.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on his experience with the New York Knicks
quotes.excerpt: The first all-Black team, you know what they were called? The New York Niggerbockers.

text_blocks.speaker: Lionel Hollins
text_blocks.text: There was a lot of strife between the best players, Jeff Petrie and Sidney Wicks, both great players. And so we, I was like, this is the NBA. And then the first thing that happened was, we in the locker room and dude pulls out a cigarette, starts smoking in the locker room. That was the climate of the locker room. And then somebody said, man, let me get a light from your smokes. Anybody, yo, you got a smoke over there for me? Right? And we got three or four guys smoking in the locker room.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: And I'm like, this the NBA, and then the fighting at practice all the time. And people competed hard because the salaries weren't big. And if you were the last two or three guys and you were Black, and there was two or three white guys that were there, those three Black guys were gone.

text_blocks.speaker: Lionel Hollins
text_blocks.text: They weren't going to have an all-Black team. The first all-Black team, you know what they were called? The New York Niggerbockers.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on the importance of winning a championship
quotes.excerpt: That's what everybody strives for to reach the top of your profession and be called champions.

text_blocks.speaker: Lionel Hollins
text_blocks.text: What it meant to me was a lot because that's what everybody strives for to reach the top of your profession and be called champions. The thing that I learned real quick was, as soon as you won it, everybody's like, are you going to do it next year? Right? Show me state. Right, right. And then when you go through the next year and you have some stumbles during the season, everybody, oh, they can't do it, blah, blah, blah.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: But it it it showed you what you're made of because you got to go through a lot.

quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on coaching players to be mature in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: If you come in the league at 19 and you're the same person at 36, then you just wasted all those years.
quotes.quote: If you come in the league at 19 and you're the same person at 36, then you just wasted all those years. It's about growing. I always say, if you come in the league at 19 and you're the same person at 36, then you just wasted all those years. Because it's about growing.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on the changing nature of NBA coaching and player roles
quotes.excerpt: The strategy of plays and making people think is lost.
quotes.quote: The strategy of plays and making people think is lost. I think it's easier to coach players in the general sense of basketball because you know where to stand, you know to come off the H.O., pass it up top, go screen, come back out. It's so simple, but the strategy of plays and making people think is lost.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on the lack of secondary options in modern NBA plays
quotes.excerpt: You don't see any plays anymore except for pick and roll or a slip of a pick and roll.
quotes.quote: You don't see any plays anymore except for pick and roll or a slip of a pick and roll. It's the way it is. I think it's easier to coach players in the general sense of basketball because you know where to stand. You know to come off the H.O., pass it up top, go screen, come back out. It's so simple, but the strategy of plays and making people think is lost.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on the importance of not quitting as a player
quotes.excerpt: You didn't quit. You didn't lay down and become a victim. You found a way to get up and keep moving.
quotes.quote: You didn't quit. You didn't lay down and become a victim. You found a way to get up and keep moving. And I think we're losing that in our society, and we're losing it in basketball. There's a lot of kids, as soon as the game gets down 15, 20, unless they can make threes, they quit. They just flat quit.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on the importance of player resilience
quotes.excerpt: Every level has the same concept and foundation, fundamentals, playing together, playing hard.
quotes.quote: Every level has the same concept and foundation, fundamentals, playing together, playing hard. Learn those fundamentals, learn how to teach them, learn how to communicate with your team. And the last thing is, figure out who your players are, both as players and as people. That's important.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on the importance of knowing your players
quotes.excerpt: When you go coaching, you don't know anybody, but you got to find out quick.
quotes.quote: When you go coaching, you don't know anybody, but you got to find out quick. And when you go to practice, you got to find out quick who can play. It's like I told somebody this story, Z. I said, we ran, get it in, because we knew they were going to foul. We were ready for you, because I knew you were going to walk up there and make two free throws.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on the NBA as an entertainment business
quotes.excerpt: It's all about entertainment, how much money can be made.
quotes.quote: It's all about entertainment, how much money can be made. I mean, look at all the different streaming avenues that the NBA has signed up with. You can watch a game almost anywhere now, but you got to pay for it. And the players all think it's entertainment.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on the importance of not being a showman
quotes.excerpt: I'm not dancing. I'm down 20 points and I make a dunk, I'm not dancing.
quotes.quote: I'm not dancing. I'm down 20 points and I make a dunk, I'm not dancing. I'm trying to still get back in the game. But that's the way it is, and you got guys just want to be entertainers. They want the branding and the notoriety and all that stuff.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on his coaching style and intensity
quotes.excerpt: I was quiet, and you know I'm pretty quiet. But when it was competition, I was trying to breathe in their nostrils so they were breathing my air.
quotes.quote: I was quiet, and you know I'm pretty quiet. But when it was competition, I was trying to breathe in their nostrils so they were breathing my air.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on the importance of not giving players the floor
quotes.excerpt: Don't ever give a player the floor if you think he's upset.
quotes.quote: Don't ever give a player the floor if you think he's upset. Okay, I was a part of where they got to duking because somebody called out somebody else. Right. Right, you know, like, no, don't do that. You talk, you do all the talking. Hey, you know, I love you. You don't need to be that way.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on the importance of not holding onto problems
quotes.excerpt: Whenever I had a problem with any of you, once I voiced it, it was over. I never held onto a problem.
quotes.quote: Whenever I had a problem with any of you, once I voiced it, it was over. I never held onto a problem. And I don't think you guys did either. So we had some guys that might have that played on the team for a while, but for the most part, everybody understood. And I always believe if you're one way all the time, then players can get used to it.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on his experience coaching in Vancouver
quotes.excerpt: It was one of the best cities in North America, very cosmopolitan city, a lot of nice restaurants, beautiful scenery.
quotes.quote: It was one of the best cities in North America, very cosmopolitan city, a lot of nice restaurants, beautiful scenery. And I enjoyed being there from that perspective, but it was hard because I'm a competitor. We won 15 games the first year and we won 14 the next year.
